To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) there is no strong constraint limiting combinatorial assembly in E. coli promoters, 2) overlapping TF binding sites are found equally associated with equivalent and opposite effects on gene expression, 3) in silico designed overlapping operators are functional, and 4) synthetic promoters containing overlapping operators can be used to expand the logic of bacterial gene expression

(1) there are no clear rules limiting the combinatorics of TF binding sites at E. coli promoters, and (2) overlapping binding sites can be designed to generate synthetic regulatory circuits with complex logic
i) overlapping operators are common at E. coli promoters; ii) they can be engineered using an evolutionary algorithm; and iii) synthetic overlapping operators can be used to control gene expression
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and characterization of synthetic promoters for gene regulation in bacteria.
the design of synthetic regulatory circuits for the control of gene expression in bacteria.
the design of synthetic regulatory networks in the model bacterium E. coli.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combinatorial logic of promoter regulation is much more flexible than what has been assumed so far.
overlapping binding sites for GRs are not uncommon in E. coli and can be used for the engineering of complex synthetic promoters.

the combinatorial arrangement of TF binding sites is not constrained in the genome, and that overlapping binding sites are found equally associated with either equivalent or opposite effects on promoter activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we were able to demonstrate that overlapping binding sites for global regulators are functional in E. coli, and that they can be designed in silico and validated in vivo.
we are able to design overlapping binding sites for GRs of E. coli.
we can expand the logic of bacterial promoter by engineering overlapping operators for GRs.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the logic of bacterial transcription regulation is not limited by the combinatorial arrangement of TFs and that overlapping binding sites can be used to expand the repertoire of promoters and their regulatory logic.
the combinatorial arrangement of TF pairs in bacterial promoters is not limited by the need of equivalent effects on the target gene.
overlapping operators are not a rare event in bacterial promoters.
